extra.message: DOM-based XSS: the dangerouslySetInnerHTML prop is assigned the return value of createInnerHTML(), which is { __html: decodeURIComponent(document.location.hash) }. The URL fragment is fully attacker-controlled (e.g. a crafted link like .../dom-xss#, exactly as the SAMPLE_ATTACK constant on line 6 demonstrates) and is injected as raw HTML into the DOM without any sanitization, allowing arbitrary JavaScript execution in the context of the page.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Tainted source for DOM XSS: createInnerHTML() reads document.location.hash (attacker-controlled URL fragment), passes it through decodeURIComponent (which defeats naive percent-encoding of the payload), and returns it as the __html property intended for dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Because this value flows unsanitized into an HTML injection sink on line 54, an attacker can execute arbitrary script by directing a victim to a crafted URL. The repository's react-policy.mydsl explicitly declares this exact source/propagator/sink flow as the dom_xss vulnerability.
